quests.title: Teacup Weather Window Visit
quests.visitSkill: turning a shared pretend choice into a clear setting detail
quests.visitFit: 15-minute adult-led printable visit quest for a grandparent, relative, neighbor-helper, library table, or homeschool co-op family day.
quests.adultSetup: Print one page, place pencils between partners, and remind everyone that all weather clues and helpers are invented for Teacup Town.
quests.kidDirection: Choose a tiny weather clue, listen to one pretend helper idea, and write the first small scene.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer two imagined weather choices, such as toast fog or button rain, then ask which helper should check the spoon window.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The spoon window shows weather shaped like ____________________.
The teacup room has a tiny sound: ____________________.
The first forecast card says ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The visiting helper suggests checking ____________________.
I choose the Teacup Town helper called ____________________.
Our made-up weather job is to ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: First, the helper looks through ____________________.
Next, the weather clue drifts toward ____________________.
The helper says, "I can fix this by ____________________."

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The clearest weather detail we invented was ____________________.
One word I want to keep in the story is ____________________.
The next Teacup Town errand could be ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: skip talking and draw one window clue, then label it ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Continue the Teacup Town scene when the forecast card changes to ____________________.

quests.title: Spoon Ferry Lunchbox Visit
quests.visitSkill: writing a beginning-middle-ending route from an invented conversation choice
quests.visitFit: 16-minute screen-free visit quest for a family visit table, library drop-in, neighbor-helper activity, or homeschool co-op writing station.
quests.adultSetup: Print the ferry page, draw a simple harbor line if useful, and keep the talk about pretend cargo, pretend cafes, and story choices.
quests.kidDirection: Send the spoon ferry across Lunchbox Harbor, choose one cargo, and write three gentle route steps.
quests.hostPrompt: Name two pretend ferry cargo choices, then ask which dock should receive the first polite note.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The spoon ferry waits beside the dock called ____________________.
The lunchbox harbor cargo is ____________________.
The water makes a soft sound like ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The visiting helper thinks the ferry should stop at ____________________.
I choose the cargo helper named ____________________.
The polite dock question is ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: First, the ferry carries ____________________.
Next, the helper asks, "Do you need ____________________?"
Last, the dock note explains ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The best route word from this visit is ____________________.
The harbor detail I can picture clearly is ____________________.
The next ferry stop could be ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: trace the harbor path silently and fill one cargo label: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Add one more ferry sentence about the dock shaped like ____________________.

quests.title: Pocket Park Notice Visit
quests.visitSkill: turning an invented notice into a helpful character line
quests.visitFit: 15-minute cooperative printable quest for grandparent visits, relative visits, library family tables, or co-op family writing days.
quests.adultSetup: Print one page, offer a pencil, and invite only pretend park notices about tiny jobs, picnic lists, seed swaps, or bench clues.
quests.kidDirection: Make a tiny notice, choose a pocket park helper, and write what the helper says after reading it.
quests.hostPrompt: Offer two pretend notice ideas, then let the child choose which one belongs on the matchbox board.

pageSections.heading: Visit story seed
lines: The matchbox notice board asks for ____________________.
The notice is pinned beside ____________________.
The pocket park bench is made from ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Talk-to-story choice
lines: The visiting helper suggests a notice about ____________________.
I choose the park helper called ____________________.
The helper brings a tiny object: ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Tiny draft
lines: First, the helper reads ____________________.
Next, the helper says, "I can help by ____________________."
Then the park path points toward ____________________.

pageSections.heading: Visit wrap
lines: The notice word that helped our story was ____________________.
The helper's kind action was ____________________.
The next pocket park notice could ask for ____________________.

quests.quietOption: Quiet option: write only the notice headline and add one park doodle label: ____________________.
quests.takeHomeLine: Take-home line: Continue the Pocket Park story with a new notice about ____________________.

quests.title: Button Bakery Map Visit
quests.visitSkill: using adult talk to revise one map clue into a clearer direction
quests.visitFit: 17-minute adult-led printable visit quest for relative visits, neighbor-helper visits, library family tables, and homeschool co-op stations.
quests.adultSetup: Print the map page, offer beside, near, around, and past as direction words, and keep every bakery clue pretend.
quests.kidDirection: Find the mixed-up crumb map, choose one clearer direction, and write the fixed bakery route.
quests.hostPrompt: Ask which pretend bakery object should be easy to find, then offer one direction word for the child to try.
